problem: The quadratic polynomial $f(x)$ has real coefficients, has roots ${x}_{1}=6\text{i}$ and ${x}_{2}=-6\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $1.$ Find $f(x).$

feedback.problem: The quadratic polynomial $f(z)$ has real coefficients, has roots ${z}_{1}=2\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=-2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $1.$ Find $f(z).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${z}_{1}=2\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=-2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(z-{z}_{1})(z-{z}_{2}) & =(1)(z-2\text{i})(z-(-2\text{i})) \\  & =(z-2\text{i})(z+2\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(z-2\text{i})(z+2\text{i}) & ={z}^{2}-(2\text{i})^{2} \\  & ={z}^{2}-4{\text{i}}^{2} \\  & ={z}^{2}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(z)={z}^{2}+4.$
